title: BNCI 2015-003 P300 dataset
description: Auditory P300 brain-computer interface speller dataset using the AMUSE (Auditory Multi-class Spatial ERP) paradigm, in which spatial auditory cues from six speakers enable text entry without visual stimuli. EEG was recorded from 8 channels in healthy participants across calibration and online spelling phases, including a dynamic stopping method in the second session. The dataset supports research on auditory ERP-based communication interfaces.
methods_description: Participants sat surrounded by six speakers at ear height (60° spacing, 65 cm radius). Each direction had a unique tone and band-pass filtered noise combination, and participants mentally counted target stimuli in a two-step hex-o-spell interface. Session 1 comprised calibration (48 trials) followed by online spelling with 15 fixed iterations; Session 2 used dynamic stopping (4-15 iterations). EEG was recorded with a BrainAmp amplifier at 256 Hz from 8 Ag/AgCl electrodes and classified with shrinkage-regularized linear discriminant analysis on spatio-temporal features.
